title: Audit Log Formatter
spec: Write a logging module that exports a main function audit(events) to format security events into readable logs. The function iterates through a list of event objects. Format a string indicating the starting time using the timestamp of the first event. If an event level is the word info, format a string combining the timestamp, the word INFO, the user, and the action. If the level is the word warning, combine the timestamp, the word WARNING, the user, and the reason. If error, combine the timestamp, the word ERROR, the error code, and the file name. If debug, combine the timestamp, the word DEBUG, the module, and the memory usage. After processing, append a summary string combining the total count of events processed and the count of errors. Finally, create a concluding string marking the end of the audit log for the date of the first event. Return an array of all these formatted strings.

title: HTML Invoice Generator
spec: Create an HTML invoice generator with the main function invoice(data). Start by creating a header string containing the invoice number and customer name. Create a table start string using the word table. Iterate over the items to create table rows. For each item, format a string for the item description, a string for the quantity, a string for the unit price formatted to two decimals, and a string for the calculated subtotal. After the loop, format a string for the grand total row. Close the table with a closing string. Create a footer string thanking the customer by name. Return an array of all the generated HTML strings.

title: API Endpoint Builder
spec: Implement a function endpoints(config) that builds API URLs based on a configuration object containing a base url, API version, and a user identifier. Create a base path string combining the base url and version. Generate a string for the user profile endpoint using the base path and user identifier. Generate a string for the user settings endpoint. Create a string for the user orders endpoint appending a query parameter for a limit. Format a string for a specific order endpoint using the user identifier and a dummy order identifier. Generate a string for the user friends endpoint. Generate a string for a search endpoint using the base path and a default query. Format a string for the logout endpoint using the base path. Return an array of all these endpoint URLs.

title: SQL Query Generator
spec: Write a function queries(schema) to generate SQL statements. The input object provides a table name, a primary key column, and an array of regular columns. Format a string for a select all query using the table name. Format a string for a select by id query using the table name and primary key. Format a string for an insert query using the table name and joining the regular columns. Format a string for the insert values placeholder using the number of columns. Format a string for an update query combining the table name and the first regular column. Format a string for a delete query using the table name and primary key. Format a string for a count query on the table name. Format a string for a drop table query using the table name. Return an array containing these generated SQL strings.

title: Markdown Profile Builder
spec: Implement a markdown builder with the function profile(user). The input object has fields for username, full name, location, age, occupation, website, and a list of hobbies. Generate a main heading string with the full name and username. Generate a subheading string for the location and age. Create a string for the occupation section. Format a link string for the website. Create a string starting a list of hobbies. Iterate through the hobbies and create a formatted list item string for each hobby name. Format a footer string with the current year and username. Format a contact string with a simulated email address based on the username and a default domain. Return a single joined string separated by newlines.

title: Server Provisioning Script
spec: Create a function script(server) that generates a sequence of shell commands to provision a linux server. The input object has an ip address, admin user, application name, database name, and port number. Generate a string for an ssh login command using the admin user and ip address. Generate a string to create a directory for the application name. Format a string to set permissions on that directory for the admin user. Create a string to configure the firewall for the given port number. Format a string to create a database with the database name. Generate a string to grant privileges on that database to the admin user. Format a string to start a service matching the application name. Create a string to echo a success message containing the application name and ip address. Return an array of these command strings.

title: System Metrics Reporter
spec: Write a function metrics(stats) that generates a text report from server statistics. The input contains a server name, uptime in days, cpu usage percentage, memory usage in gigabytes, disk space in terabytes, network speed, and active connections. Format a title string with the server name. Format a string showing the uptime in days. Create a string for the cpu usage percentage warning if it exceeds a threshold. Format a string for the memory usage. Create a string for the disk space. Format a string for the network speed in megabits. Create a string for the active connections count. Format a concluding summary string combining the server name and the word healthy. Return an array of these report lines.

title: Project File Path Constructor
spec: Implement paths(project) to construct standard project directory paths. The input object contains a root directory path, a project name, and a version string. Format a string for the main source folder combining the root and the word source. Create a string for the compiled output folder using the root and the word build. Format a string for the assets folder using the root and the word public. Create a string for the main index html file inside the assets folder. Format a string for the main stylesheet inside the assets folder. Create a string for the configuration json file in the root directory named after the project. Format a string for the readme markdown file combining the project name and version. Format a string for the log file path inside the root directory. Return an array of all generated file paths.

title: Email Campaign Builder
spec: Create an email campaign generator with the function campaign(details). The input provides a recipient name, a product name, a discount percentage, a promo code, an expiration date, and a sender name. Generate a subject line string featuring the product name and discount percentage. Format a greeting string using the recipient name. Create a string introducing the product name. Format a string highlighting the promo code and the discount percentage. Create a string mentioning the expiration date. Format a call to action string with a fabricated web link containing the promo code. Generate a sign off string using the sender name. Create a footer string with an unsubscribe link containing the recipient name. Return an array of the email lines.

title: Dockerfile Generator
spec: Write a function dockerfile(config) that generates lines for a container build file. The input contains a base image, a maintainer name, an application directory, an environment variable, an exposed port, a start command, and a package to install. Generate a from string using the base image. Format a maintainer string with the maintainer name. Create a work directory string using the application directory. Format an environment string setting the environment variable to the word production. Generate a run string to update and install the specified package. Format a copy string for the application files. Create an expose string using the exposed port. Generate a command string using the start command. Return the lines as an array of strings.

title: CSS Theme Generator
spec: Implement a style generator using stylesheet(theme). The input object contains primary color, secondary color, base font size, heading font size, margin size, padding size, and border radius. Generate a string for the body selector setting the background to the primary color. Format a string for text color using the secondary color. Create a string for paragraph font size using the base font size. Format a string for heading size using the heading font size. Generate a string for a container class setting the margin to the margin size. Create a string for the container padding using the padding size. Format a string for button border radius using the border radius. Format a string for a hover state pseudo class using the primary color. Return the generated rules as an array of strings.

title: Graphviz DOT Network
spec: Create a function graph(network) to generate a directed graph representation in the dot language. The input has a graph name, an array of node objects each with an identifier and a label, and an array of edge objects each with a source, destination, and weight. Format a string to start a directed graph using the graph name. Iterate through the nodes and format a string for each assigning the label to the identifier. Iterate through the edges and format a string for each connecting the source to the destination. Inside the edge loop format a string to set the weight label. Format a string to set a default node shape to the word circle. Format a string to set a default edge color to the word blue. Format a string to close the graph structure. Format a string describing the total count of nodes and edges as a comment. Return all strings as an array.

title: FFmpeg Command Builder
spec: Implement execute(options) to build command line execution strings for a media encoder. The input contains an input file, an output file, a video codec, an audio codec, a bitrate, a resolution, and a preset. Format a string for the basic executable command. Create a string for the input file flag using the input file path. Format a string for the video codec flag. Generate a string for the audio codec flag. Create a string for the bitrate parameter. Format a string for the resolution scale parameter. Create a string for the preset speed flag. Generate a string for the output file path. Return an array of all these flag strings.

title: AI System Prompt Generator
spec: Write a function prompt(context) that builds a system instruction prompt. The input provides a bot persona, a user name, a target language, a conversation topic, a maximum word count, a tone, and a specific rule. Format a string defining the bot persona. Create a greeting string that uses the user name. Format a string instructing the bot to speak in the target language. Generate a string restricting the focus to the conversation topic. Create a string enforcing the maximum word count constraint. Format a string requesting the specified tone. Generate a string highlighting the specific rule. Format a concluding string confirming the parameters. Return these instructions as an array of strings.

title: CSV Grade Report Builder
spec: Create a function export(records) to generate a text report. The input is an array of student objects containing identifier, first name, last name, grade level, and grade point average. Format a string for the report title. Format a string for the column headers. Iterate over records and format a string for the full name. Format a string for the student row combining identifier and full name. Format a string for a detailed row adding grade level and the grade point average. Format a string for an evaluation sentence using the full name and grade point average. After the loop, format a string for the total count of students processed. Format a string for the generation date using the current year. Return an array containing all generated strings.

title: Regex Pattern Builder
spec: Write a function regex(pattern) that constructs components for a complex text matching pattern. The input object contains a prefix string, a core word, a suffix string, a minimum length number, a maximum length number, and a file extension. Format a string to match the prefix at the start of a line. Create a string to match the core word ignoring case. Format a string to match the suffix at the end of a line. Generate a string defining a length quantifier using the minimum and maximum length numbers. Create a string to match the literal file extension. Format a string combining the prefix and core word in a non capturing group. Format a string creating a positive lookahead for the suffix. Generate a string for a fallback pattern using the core word. Return an array of these pattern strings.

title: Omnichannel Notifier
spec: Implement a message formatter with the function notify(alert). The input contains an event type, a user name, a device name, a time string, a location, and a severity level. Format a string for a text message including the event type and severity level. Create a string for a mobile push notification using the user name and device name. Format a string for an email subject line featuring the event type and time string. Generate a string for the email body combining the user name, event type, and location. Format a string for a desktop pop up using the device name and severity level. Create a string for a chat channel alert using the user name and event type. Format a string for a log entry combining all six fields. Generate a string for an audio screen reader using the event type and user name. Return an array of all formatted messages.

title: SVG Bar Chart
spec: Create a function chart(data) that builds scalable vector graphics strings for a bar chart. The input contains a chart title, a total width, a total height, and an array of objects each with a label and a value. Format a string for the opening svg tag using the width and height. Create a string for a text element containing the chart title. Iterate through the array to generate bars. For each item, format a string for a rectangle element calculating its height based on the value. Format a string for a text element placing the label below the rectangle. Format a string for a text element placing the value inside the rectangle. After the loop, format a string for a bounding box rectangle using the width and height. Generate a string for a horizontal axis line. Create a string for the closing svg tag. Return an array of these graphical strings.

title: REST API Response Formatter
spec: Write a utility function response(result) that constructs string messages for an application programming interface. The input object has a status code, a status text, a resource name, a resource identifier, and an error message. Format a string for a general success message using the status code and status text. Create a string for a resource created message using the resource name and identifier. Format a string for a resource updated message using the resource name and identifier. Generate a string for a resource deleted message using the resource identifier. Create a string for a client error using the status code and error message. Format a string for a server error using the status code and resource name. Generate a string for a not found error using the resource name and identifier. Format a string for an unauthorized error using the resource name. Return an array of these response strings.

title: Makefile Generator
spec: Implement a function makefile(build) that creates build instructions for a software project. The input provides a compiler name, compiler flags, a target executable name, a source directory, an object directory, and an installation path. Format a string to define the compiler variable using the compiler name. Create a string for the flags variable using the compiler flags. Format a string for the target rule using the target executable name. Generate a string for compiling source files from the source directory into the object directory. Create a string for the clean rule targeting the object directory. Format a string for an install rule using the target executable name and the installation path. Generate a string for an uninstall rule removing the target from the installation path. Format a string listing phony targets. Return an array of these configuration strings.

title: Redis Cache Command Builder
spec: Create a function cache(operation) to construct string commands for a key value data store. The input contains a namespace, a key name, a string value, an expiry time in seconds, an increment amount, and a list name. Format a string for a set command combining the namespace, key name, and string value. Create a string for a get command using the namespace and key name. Format a string for an expire command using the key name and expiry time. Generate a string for an increment command using the key name and increment amount. Create a string for a list push command using the list name and string value. Format a string for a list range command using the list name. Generate a string for a delete command using the namespace and key name. Format a string for a ping command with the string value. Return an array of these command strings.

title: ORM Model Scaffolding
spec: Write a function scaffold(entity) that creates boilerplate code for a database model. The input object has a class name, a table name, a primary key name, and an array of property names. Format a string defining the class declaration using the class name. Create a string for a static property setting the table name. Format a string for a static property setting the primary key name. Iterate over the property names and format a string for a getter method for each property. Format a string for a setter method for each property. Format a string for a save method mentioning the table name. Generate a string for a delete method mentioning the primary key name. Format a string for a string representation method returning the class name and primary key name. Return an array of these code lines.

title: Nginx Proxy Configuration
spec: Implement a function proxy(server) that creates reverse proxy configuration lines. The input provides a domain name, a listen port, a backend upstream address, a log file path, an ssl certificate path, and an ssl key path. Format a string for the server block opening. Create a string to set the listen directive using the listen port. Format a string for the server name directive using the domain name. Generate a string for the access log directive using the log file path. Create a string for the ssl certificate directive using the ssl certificate path. Format a string for the ssl key directive using the ssl key path. Generate a string for the location block forwarding requests to the backend upstream address. Format a string setting a proxy header with the domain name. Return an array of these configuration strings.

title: RSS Feed XML Builder
spec: Create an xml generator using the function feed(channel). The input contains a blog title, a blog link, a description, an author name, and an array of post objects each having a title, link, and date. Format a string for the xml declaration. Create a string for the opening rss tag. Format a string for the channel title using the blog title. Generate a string for the channel link using the blog link. Create a string for the channel description. Iterate through the posts and generate a string for each item opening. Format a string for the post title. Format a string for the post link. Format a string for the post date. After the loop, format a string for the closing channel and rss tags using the author name in a comment. Return an array of the generated tags.

title: Test Assertion Formatter
spec: Write a function assert(test) that builds failure messages for an automated testing library. The input object contains a module name, a function name, an expected value, an actual value, an execution time, and an error type. Format a string stating the test failure combining the module name and function name. Create a string detailing the expected value. Format a string detailing the actual value. Generate a string showing the difference between expected and actual values. Create a string warning about the execution time. Format a string highlighting the error type thrown. Generate a string for a stack trace header using the function name. Format a concluding string advising to check the module name documentation. Return an array of these diagnostic strings.

title: AWS IAM Policy Generator
spec: Write a function `policy(rules)` that accepts a list of rule objects. Each rule object has a resource string, an action list, and an effect string. The function must build an access control policy document string manually. It should have a helper to format the version header, a helper to format each statement block with its specific actions, and a main driver that joins them. Build distinct strings for the policy header, the version declaration, the statement array opening, the statement identifier line, the effect declaration, the action array opening, the specific action items, the resource line, and the closing brackets. Example input: a list with one rule for an object bucket and read actions. Output: a properly indented string containing the entire policy statement.

title: Git Hook Script Builder
spec: Create a function `hook(config)` that generates a pre commit bash script. The configuration object contains a project name, a linter command, a branch prefix, and a warning message. Create helpers to build the header, the branch checking logic which compares the current branch against the allowed prefix, and the linting execution block. You must construct separate strings for the bash header, the strict mode declaration, the branch variable assignment, the branch check condition, the branch error message, the lint command variable, the lint execution block, and the lint error output. Example input: a project named frontend, branch prefix feature, and a code formatting command. Output: a complete bash script as a string.

title: Prometheus Alert Rules Generator
spec: Write a function `alerts(thresholds)` that accepts a list of monitoring definitions. Each definition contains a metric name, a warning limit, a critical limit, and an application identifier. Create helpers to generate the rule group header, the warning alert definition, and the critical alert definition. Assemble distinct strings for the group name declaration, the evaluation interval, the warning alert name, the warning expression, the warning duration, the warning labels, the critical alert name, the critical expression, and the critical annotations. Example input: a memory metric with a warning limit of eighty and critical of ninety for an app named backend. Output: a formatted monitoring rules string.

title: Kubernetes YAML Manifest Generator
spec: Provide a function `manifest(service)` that produces a deployment and networking string for a containerized application. The service object includes an application name, a container image, a port number, and a replica count. Write helper functions to generate the deployment metadata block, the pod template specification, and the networking service block. You will need to construct strings for the api version headers, the resource kind declarations, the metadata name line, the application labels, the replicas count, the container name, the container image definition, the port mappings, and the selector matches. Example input: an app named web using a proxy image with port eighty and two replicas. Output: a single string with both manifests separated by dashes.

title: HAProxy Config Generator
spec: Implement a function `haproxy(setup)` that builds a load balancer configuration file. The setup object contains a frontend port, a backend name, and a list of server objects which each have a name and an address. Define helpers to create the global defaults section, the frontend binding section, and the backend server list. The logic must build strings for the global timeout setting, the frontend binding directive, the default backend assignment, the frontend closing, the backend definition header, the balance algorithm, the server check interval, and each individual server line with its host and port. Example input: frontend port eighty, backend name web servers, and two backend hosts. Output: a multi line plain text configuration string.

title: Elasticsearch Mapping Builder
spec: Write a function `mapping(schema)` that generates an index definition string for a search engine. The schema object contains an index name, a shard count, and a list of field definitions where each has a name and a data type. Use helpers to build the settings block with the shard configuration, the mappings wrapper, and the individual property definitions. You must construct strings for the index route path, the settings opening, the shard setting line, the mappings wrapper, the properties wrapper, the field name key, the field type assignment, and the closing braces. Example input: an index named users with three shards and fields for email as keyword and age as integer. Output: a string representing the complete configuration payload.

title: GraphQL Schema Generator
spec: Provide a function `schema(models)` that takes a list of data model definitions to produce a complete type definition string. Each model has a name, a description, and a list of property objects containing a name, a type, and a required flag. Create helpers to generate the type declaration header, the individual field lines, and a root query type. Construct separate strings for the schema opening, the type documentation comment, the type declaration line, the required field definition, the optional field definition, the root query wrapper, the query resolver signature, and the schema closing. Example input: a user model with a required identifier and an optional alias. Output: a formatted schema definition string.

title: Tmux Session Script Builder
spec: Implement a function `session(layout)` that generates a shell script to automate a terminal multiplexer setup. The layout object defines a session name, a base directory, and a list of window objects each containing a name and a startup command. Write helpers to generate the session initialization command, the window creation commands, and the command execution lines. You will build strings for the bash shebang, the session existence check, the new session creation, the target directory change, the new window creation, the window renaming command, the send keys execution, and the final session attach directive. Example input: a session named dev with two windows running an editor and a server. Output: a bash script string that starts the environment.

title: Ical Event Generator
spec: Write a function `calendar(events)` that builds a standard calendar data file string. The events list contains objects with a unique identifier, a start timestamp, an end timestamp, a summary, and an organizer email. Create helpers to construct the calendar header and footer, the event start and end block, and the property lines for timestamps and summaries. Build distinct strings for the begin calendar tag, the version property, the begin event tag, the unique identifier line, the organizer property, the summary line, the start timestamp, the end timestamp, and the closing tags. Example input: one meeting event with a start time, end time, and a planning summary. Output: a formatted multi line string ready to be saved as a calendar file.

title: Sitemap XML Builder
spec: Provide a function `sitemap(pages)` that generates an XML document for search engines. The pages list contains objects that have a relative path, a priority number, and an update frequency string. Write helpers to output the standard XML declaration, the URL set opening tag, and the individual URL entries. Construct strings for the XML declaration header, the URL set opening tag, the URL wrapper opening, the full location path, the priority tag, the change frequency tag, the last modified date tag, the URL wrapper closing, and the URL set closing. Example input: a list with a home page at the root path and a contact page. Output: a full XML document string.

title: Ansible Playbook Generator
spec: Create a function `playbook(tasks)` that formats a configuration management script. The tasks list contains objects with a task name, a package name, and a desired state like present or absent. Use helpers to build the host targeting header, the tasks list declaration, and the individual package module blocks. Assemble separate strings for the document start marker, the hosts targeting line, the become privilege escalation line, the gather facts toggle, the tasks list declaration, the task name description, the package module definition, and the state parameter line. Example input: a list containing a task to install a web server package. Output: a valid script string.

title: VCF Contact Card Builder
spec: Write a function `contacts(people)` that generates a virtual contact file string from a list of user profiles. Each profile contains a first name, a last name, a phone number, an email address, and an organization name. Implement helpers to construct the begin tags, the formatted name properties, the telephone properties, the email properties, and the organization properties. Build distinct strings for the begin card tag, the version declaration, the full name line, the structured name line, the work phone line, the home phone line, the internet email line, the organization property, and the end card tag. Example input: a list of one person named john doe working at a factory. Output: a text string conforming to the standard contact format.

title: PlantUML Sequence Diagram Builder
spec: Implement a function `diagram(interactions)` that outputs a text based sequence diagram string. The interactions list holds objects with a sender, a receiver, a message, and a synchronous flag. Create helpers to generate the diagram start tag, the participant definitions, the message arrows which differ based on the synchronous flag, and the diagram end tag. Construct strings for the start tag, the title declaration, the actor participant declaration, the database participant declaration, the solid arrow for synchronous calls, the dotted arrow for asynchronous calls, the message labels, the activation block, and the end tag. Example input: a client sending a request to a server synchronously, then the server logging asynchronously. Output: a complete diagram script.

title: Systemd Service File Generator
spec: Provide a function `service(config)` that builds an initialization unit file. The configuration object includes a unit description, an execution path, a working directory, a user name, and an environment profile. Write helpers to construct the unit section, the service section, and the install section. Build strings for the unit section header, the description line, the after network dependency, the service section header, the execution start command, the working directory path, the user assignment, the environment file include, and the wanted by target. Example input: a node application running under a dedicated user account. Output: a standard unit file string.

title: Apache Virtual Host Builder
spec: Write a function `vhost(domain)` that creates a web server configuration block. The domain object contains a server name, an alias list, a document root path, and an admin email. Implement helpers to format the virtual host opening tag, the server identity lines, the directory access controls, and the logging paths. Generate separate strings for the virtual host opening tag, the port eighty binding, the server name directive, the server alias list, the server admin line, the document root assignment, the directory allow override directive, the error log path, and the custom log path. Example input: a primary domain example com with an alias. Output: a multi line configuration string.

title: Webpack Config Snippet Generator

The settings object has an entry file path, an output directory, an output filename, and a list of loader objects specifying file extensions. Define helpers to output the module exports wrapper, the entry and output block, and the rules array for the loaders. Build distinct strings for the module exports wrapper, the mode declaration, the entry point assignment, the output path resolution, the output filename definition, the module rules wrapper, the regular expression for file testing, the loader assignment, and the closing brackets. title: GitHub Actions Workflow Builder
spec: Implement a function `workflow(pipeline)` that generates a continuous integration definition file. The pipeline object contains a workflow name, a trigger branch, an operating system environment, and a list of step commands. Use helpers to generate the trigger section, the jobs header, the runner environment definition, and the execution steps. Construct strings for the workflow name line, the push branch trigger array, the jobs definition header, the build job name, the runs on directive, the steps array header, the checkout step use directive, the individual run commands, and the environment variable pass. title: Logstash Pipeline Builder
spec: Write a function `pipeline(config)` that constructs a data processing configuration string. The configuration specifies an input port, a match pattern, a date field to parse, and an output host address. Create helpers to build the input section, the filter section applying the pattern and date parsing, and the output section routing to a database. Build separate strings for the pipeline input header, the tcp port assignment, the pipeline filter header, the match rule, the date match array, the pipeline output header, the database host definition, the index naming pattern, and the closing braces. Write helpers to construct the header block, the environment table, the numbered steps list, and the conclusion section. title: DNS Zone File Generator

Implement helpers to generate the origin directive, the authority record, the name server records, and the address records. Construct strings for the origin directive, the time to live definition, the start of authority header, the serial number line, the refresh interval line, the retry interval line, the name server assignment, the primary host to ip mapping, and the secondary host mapping. Example input: a domain with a web host and a mail host. Output: a standard zone file text string.

title: Rsync Backup Script Builder
spec: Write a function `backup(job)` that produces a shell script for synchronizing directories. The job object defines a source path, a destination host, a destination path, a secure key file, and an exclude pattern. Create helpers to build the script header, the logging setup, the synchronization command, and the completion notification. Build distinct strings for the bash interpreter line, the strict error handling line, the log file definition, the source path variable, the destination path variable, the secure shell command argument, the exclusion flag, the main synchronization command, and the completion success message. title: Firewall Rule Generator
spec: Implement a function `firewall(policies)` that generates a shell script to configure network rules. The policies list contains objects with a protocol, a port number, a source ip range, and an action like accept or drop. Write helpers to construct the flush existing rules command, the default policy commands, and the specific port rules. Construct separate strings for the interpreter shebang, the flush existing rules command, the default input drop line, the default forward drop line, the default output accept line, the loopback accept rule, the specific protocol flag, the destination port flag, and the jump action flag. title: Database Aggregation Pipeline Stringifier
spec: Provide a function `aggregation(query)` that formats a database query pipeline into a readable code string for documentation purposes. The query object has a match collection name, a group field, a sum alias, and a sort order. Create helpers to build the match stage string, the group stage string, and the sort stage string. Construct strings for the collection pipeline wrapper, the match stage opening, the match condition syntax, the group stage opening, the group identifier mapping, the accumulator function syntax, the sort stage opening, the sort direction line, and the array closing brackets. Example input: a query filtering active users and grouping them by region. Output: a string representation of the pipeline.

title: Cron Job Schedule Builder
spec: Write a function `schedule(tasks)` that creates a system task file string. The tasks list contains objects with minute, hour, day, month, and weekday expressions, along with an execution command and an output log file. Implement helpers to generate the environment variable header, the individual task schedule lines, and the output redirection logic. Build distinct strings for the shell environment assignment, the path variable assignment, the mail notification assignment, the task comment description, the timing expression columns, the command execution path, the standard output redirection, the error output redirection, and the newline separator. Example input: a daily cleanup script running at midnight. Output: a formatted schedule file string.

title: Terraform Resource Builder
spec: Create a function `terraform(infrastructure)` that constructs a declarative configuration string for cloud resources. The infrastructure object includes a region, a virtual network name, an address space, and a list of subnet objects containing a name and a prefix. Write helpers to generate the provider block, the virtual network resource block, and the subnet inline blocks. Construct separate strings for the terraform block, the provider region assignment, the resource type declaration, the resource name identifier, the network address space array, the subnet block opening, the subnet name assignment, the subnet address prefix, and the closing braces. Example input: a network in the east region with two subnets. Output: a formatted configuration string.

title: Bibtex Entry Builder
spec: Write a script to generate a bibliography text format given an array of publication records. Implement `format(publications)`. Each publication has a type, an author string, a title, a year, a publisher, a journal, and a volume. For a book type, return a string starting with an at symbol followed by book, open brace, then a unique key formed by the first author last name and the year. On the next lines, output author equals the author, title equals the title, publisher equals the publisher, and year equals the year, closing with a brace. For an article type, return an at symbol followed by article, the unique key, and lines for author, title, journal, volume, and year. For a generic type, output an at symbol followed by misc and the basic fields. Append a newline after each entry. Example: an input with a book by Smith in 2020 titled History returns a formatted text block mapping those attributes to bibliography fields.

title: Manual Page Source Builder
spec: Create a generator that produces formatted source text for system manual pages. Provide `manual(command)`. The command object has a name, a section number, a date, a short description, an array of options, and an author string. The output must begin with a line starting with a dot and the letters TH, followed by the name, section number, and date. Next, output a line with a dot and SH followed by the word NAME. On the next line, combine the name, a hyphen, and the short description. Output a dot and SH followed by SYNOPSIS, then a line displaying the name and an options placeholder. Output a dot and SH followed by OPTIONS. For each option, output a dot and IP with the option flag, then output a line containing the option description. Finally, output a dot and SH followed by AUTHOR, and output the author string. Return the complete string separating commands with newlines.

title: Latex Document Scaffolder
spec: Write a module to generate a basic typesetting markup document from a content specification. Provide `typeset(document)`. The document object contains a paper size, an author, a title, an abstract text, and a list of sections. Each section has a heading and an array of paragraphs. The output must begin with a document class declaration using the paper size. Next, output the title declaration and author declaration. Begin the document environment. Output a make title command. If the abstract text exists, wrap it in an abstract environment. For each section in the list, output a section command with the heading, then loop through its paragraphs and append each followed by a blank line. End the document environment at the end. Example: a letter size document by Jane titled Hello will yield a complete document string containing the appropriate markup commands and text blocks.

title: OpenVPN Config Builder
spec: Create a generator that produces virtual private network client configuration text files. Implement `configure(settings)`. The settings include a protocol, a remote host, a remote port, a cipher type, an authentication type, and strings for inline certificate authority, client certificate, and client key. The output string must start with client followed by a device type line specifying tun. Next, specify the protocol using the provided value. Specify the remote endpoint using the host and port. Add a resolv retry infinite line and a no bind line. Output a cipher line using the cipher type and an authentication line using the authentication type. Create an inline xml style block for the certificate authority containing its string, another block for the client certificate, and a third block for the client key. Return the full text with each directive on a new line.

title: Intrusion Prevention Jail Builder
spec: Write a utility to generate configuration files for a service ban manager. Implement `jail(configs)`. Each configuration has a service name, an enabled flag, a filter name, a log path, a maximum retry count, a find time window, and a ban time duration. Loop through the configurations. For each one, output the service name enclosed in square brackets. On the next lines, set enabled to true or false, and output the filter directive using the filter name. Output an action directive that specifies an ip tables rule passing the service name and the port to block. Specify the log path directive. Output the maximum retry, find time, and ban time directives using their respective values. Append an ignore ip line containing a local loopback address. Leave an empty line between blocks. Return the complete string.

title: Route Markup Generator
spec: Build a utility to generate geographic markup files from a list of waypoints. Implement `track(waypoints)`. Each waypoint provides a name, a description, a latitude, a longitude, and an altitude. The output must start with an xml declaration and a markup root element. Inside the root, open a document element. For each waypoint, open a placemark element. Add a name element with the waypoint name and a description element with the description. Add a point element containing a coordinates element formatted as longitude comma latitude comma altitude. Close the placemark element. After processing all waypoints, close the document and root elements. Return the complete formatted string. Example: an input with a single waypoint in Paris returns an xml structure containing the point and coordinates.

title: Interface Definition Generator
spec: Create a script to generate interface definition language files for a remote procedure call system. Implement `interface(schema)`. The schema specifies a namespace string, an array of includes, an array of structs, and a service definition. The output must start by declaring the namespace using the provided string. For each included file in the array, output an include statement. Next, iterate through the structs. For each struct, output a struct declaration with its name, and loop through its fields. Output each field with its numerical identifier, type, and name, ending with a semicolon. After the structs, output a service block using the service name. Inside the service, loop through its functions, outputting the return type, function name, and an argument list formatting the parameter types and names. Close all blocks and return the text.

title: Wireguard Config Builder
spec: Create a configuration file generator for a modern secure tunnel network. Implement `tunnel(config)`. The configuration contains a client private key, a listen port, an assigned address, a max transmission unit size, a domain name server, and an array of peers. A peer has a public key, an allowed ips string, an endpoint host, an endpoint port, and a persistent keepalive interval. The output must start with an interface section heading in brackets. Below it, add a private key line, an address line, a listen port line, a domain name server line, and a max transmission unit line using the provided values. Then loop over the array of peers. For each peer, output a peer section heading in brackets followed by a blank line. Add a public key line, an allowed ips line, an endpoint line joining the host and port with a colon, and a persistent keepalive line. Return the multi line text result.

title: EDI Transaction Builder
spec: Develop a module to format electronic data interchange messages for purchase orders. Implement `transaction(order)`. The order has a sender id, a receiver id, a control number, a date string, and a list of line items. Each line item has a quantity, a price, and a product code. The result string must start with an interchange header segment using the sender id, receiver id, and control number. Add a functional group header segment using the date string. Add a transaction set header segment. For each line item, output a baseline item data segment containing the quantity, price, and product code separated by asterisks. Add a transaction set trailer segment counting the line items. Add a functional group trailer and an interchange trailer. End each segment with a tilde character. Return the final string.

title: Network Scan Command Builder
spec: Write a utility to construct command line strings for network security auditing. Implement `scan(targets)`. Each target object has an ip address, an array of specific ports, a boolean for service detection, a boolean for operating system detection, a timing template number, and an output filename. For each target, begin the command with the network mapper executable name. If service detection is true, append the service version flag. If operating system detection is true, append the operating system flag. Append a timing flag combined with the timing template number. If the ports array is not empty, append a port flag followed by the ports joined by commas. Append the normal output flag followed by the output filename. Finally, append the ip address. Return a single string with each command separated by a newline.

title: Video Subtitle Track Builder
spec: Create a script to generate video text track files from caption metadata. Implement `caption(metadata)`. The metadata contains a region identifier, a region width, a region origin, and an array of subtitles. The output must begin with the web file header. On the next line, output a region definition block specifying the region identifier, the width percentage, and the origin coordinates. Loop through the array of subtitles. For each subtitle, output a sequence number based on its index. On the next line, output the start time, an arrow separator, and the end time, appending a region align attribute using the region identifier. If a speaker name is present, prefix the first text line with a voice tag using the speaker name. Output all text lines, appending a blank line after each subtitle block. Return the complete formatted string.

title: Directory Import Builder
spec: Build a generator to format text files for adding entries to a lightweight directory access protocol server. Provide `directory(entries)`. Each entry has a distinguished name, an object class array, a common name, an email address, a surname, a user password, a description string, and a telephone number. Iterate over the entries. For each entry, start with a line specifying the distinguished name. Next, add a change type line set to add. For each class in the object class array, output an object class line. Output a common name line, a surname line, and an email line using the respective values. Output a user password line containing the password. Output a description line and a telephone number line. End each entry block with an empty line. Return the full text string ready for import.

title: Cloud Resource Script Builder
spec: Write a tool to generate declarative cloud infrastructure code from a resource blueprint. Implement `infrastructure(blueprint)`. The blueprint contains a location string, an environment string, and a list of storage accounts. Each storage account has a name prefix, a redundancy sku, and an access tier. Start the output by declaring a param for location and a param for environment. For each storage account, output a resource declaration block. Create a unique name variable by combining the name prefix and the environment string. Output the provider type for storage. Inside the block, set the name property to the unique name, the location property to the location parameter, the sku name to the redundancy sku, and the kind to storage version two. Set the access tier property. Return the formatted file content.

title: Network Share Config Builder
spec: Create a generator that produces configuration files for a network file sharing daemon. Implement `sharing(settings)`. The input is a global settings object and a list of share definitions. The global settings dictate a workgroup name, a server string, a security mode, and a log file path. Begin the output with a global section heading enclosed in brackets. Set the workgroup directive, the server string directive, the security directive, and the log file directive using the global properties. Append a max log size line using a fixed number. Iterate through the share definitions. Each share provides a share name, a directory path, a valid users list, a comment string, and read only and guest ok boolean flags. For each share, output the share name in brackets. Output a comment line, a path line, and a valid users line joining the list with spaces. Convert the flags to yes or no strings for the read only and guest ok directives. Return the full text.

title: Text Processor Script Builder
spec: Write a module to generate stream editor scripts for text analysis tasks. Expose `processor(task)`. The task has a delimiter, an array of rules where each rule has a match pattern, a column number to print, and a sum column number. The script must begin with a begin block setting the field separator to the delimiter and initializing a total variable to zero. Loop through the rules. For each rule, output a rule block with its match pattern. Inside, add a print statement that outputs a fixed string, the current line number, and the field corresponding to the column number. Add an assignment adding the sum column field to the total. After the loop, output an end block printing a final string and the total. Return the single script string.

title: Mail Transfer Config Builder
spec: Build a utility to generate main configuration files for a mail transfer agent. Implement `mail(settings)`. The settings object contains a hostname, a domain name, an origin string, a list of destination domains, a network block, a relay host, and a message size limit. The output must set the my hostname directive to the hostname and my domain to the domain name. Set my origin to the origin string. Create a my destination line that lists the hostname, localhost, and all domains in the destination domains list separated by commas. Set the my networks directive to the network block and a local loopback address. If a relay host is provided, set the relay host directive enclosed in square brackets. Set the message size limit directive. Set the inet interfaces directive to all. Format each directive on a new line and return the result.

title: Log Rotation Config Builder
spec: Write a generator to produce system log management configuration files. Implement `rotation(logs)`. Each log object has a file path, a rotation frequency, a retain count, a pre rotate command, and a post rotate command. Loop through the logs. For each log, begin by outputting the file path followed by an open brace. On the next lines, output the rotation frequency, then a rotate line using the retain count, and a missing ok line. If a pre rotate command exists, open a pre rotate section, output the command on a new line, and close the section with an end script line. Do the same for a post rotate command in a post rotate section. Close the log block with a brace. Leave an empty line between configurations. Return the full text string.

title: Encryption Key Script Builder
spec: Create a script generator to automate batch generation of cryptographic keys. Implement `encryption(profiles)`. Each profile specifies a key type, a key length, an expiration duration, a real name, an email address, and an optional passphrase. For each profile, begin a block containing the standard batch generation tag. Add a key type line using the provided type and a key length line using the length. Add a subkey type line and subkey length line matching the primary key. Add a name real line with the real name and a name email line with the email address. Set an expire date line using the expiration duration. If a passphrase exists, add a passphrase line. End the block with a commit tag. Join all profiles with a blank line. Return the full script string.

title: Cluster Job Scaffolder
spec: Write a utility to generate workload orchestrator job files in declarative syntax. Provide `orchestrator(jobs)`. Each job contains an identifier, a datacenter list, a task group name, a count, a docker image, and a list of port numbers. The output must start with a job declaration using the identifier and an open brace. Inside the job block, list the datacenters formatted as an array. Open a group block with the task group name. Inside it, set the count parameter. Open a task block naming the task server, and set its driver to docker. Inside a config block, specify the image using the docker image. Open a network block. Loop through the port numbers and add a port declaration block for each using the number as the label. Close all nested blocks properly and return the formatted string.

title: Secure Shell Config Builder
spec: Create a tool to assemble client connection configurations for remote access. Expose `access(hosts)`. Each host object contains a short alias, a real hostname, a username, an identity file path, a port number, and a forward agent boolean. Iterate over the host objects. For each host, start with a line specifying the host alias. On the following lines, indent and specify the host name directive using the real hostname. Add a user directive using the username. If a port is provided, add a port directive using the port number. Add an identity file directive pointing to the path. If the forward agent boolean is true, add a forward agent directive set to yes, otherwise set it to no. Separate each host block with an empty line. Return the multiline configuration text.

title: Network Boot Menu Builder
spec: Write a utility to generate startup menu files for a network booting environment. Expose `boot(menu)`. The menu object has a default label, a timeout value, a menu title string, and a list of boot entries. The output must start by setting the default directive to the default label and the timeout directive to the timeout value. Output a menu title directive using the title string. For each boot entry, there is a label string, a kernel path, an init ram disk path, and an array of append parameters. Output a label directive using the label string. On the next lines, indent and output a kernel directive with the kernel path, followed by an append directive that lists the init ram disk path and joins the append parameters with spaces. Separate each entry block with an empty line and return the result.

title: Mail Filter Recipe Builder
spec: Create a script to build filtering rules for a local mail delivery agent. Implement `filter(rules)`. The input specifies a mail directory path, a default mailbox name, a log file path, and an array of recipe objects. Start the output by setting the mail directory variable, the default variable, and the log file variable using the provided values. Add a verbose variable set to off. Loop through the recipe objects. Each recipe has a target mailbox, a sender match string, a subject match string, and a boolean flag for dropping the message. For each recipe, output a recipe start marker composed of a colon and a zero. Output a condition line starting with an asterisk and a caret, matching the from header to the sender match string. Output another condition line matching the subject header to the subject match string. Finally, if the drop flag is true, output a path to the dev null device; otherwise, output the target mailbox string. Separate recipes with a blank line. Return the full text.

title: Database Server Config Builder
spec: Write a utility to generate initialization files for a relational database server. Implement `database(config)`. The config provides a port number, a socket path, a data directory, a max connections number, a buffer pool size, a log file path, and a list of replication peers. Begin the output with a client section heading in brackets, setting the port and socket directives. Next, add a server section heading. Output the port, socket, and data directory directives. Set the max connections and the innodb buffer pool size directives. Set the log error directive using the log file path. Loop over the replication peers. For each peer, output a server id line using its index, followed by a replicate do db line using the peer database name, and a master host line using the peer ip address. Return the complete formatted string.

title: Desktop Application Launcher Builder
spec: Build a generator to create linux desktop entry files for application menus. Define `launcher(app)`. The app object has a display name, a generic name, a comment string, an executable path, an icon path, a terminal boolean, an array of categories, and an array of mime types. The output must start with a desktop entry header in brackets. Output a type directive set to application. Output a name directive, a generic name directive, and a comment directive using their respective strings. Output an exec directive using the executable path and an icon directive using the icon path. Output a terminal directive converted to a true or false string. Join the categories array with semicolons and append a trailing semicolon for the categories directive. Do the same for the mime type directive. Return the text file content.

title: Postscript Graphic Generator
spec: Build a script to generate page description language files for drawing basic shapes. Implement `postscript(shapes)`. The input is a page width, a page height, and a list of shape objects. Begin the output with the standard postscript version header. Output a bounding box line using the width and height. Output a line to translate the origin to the center of the page. For each shape in the list, if it is a rectangle, output lines to set the rgb color, move to its starting coordinates, construct lines to its width and height, close the path, and fill it. If it is a circle, output the rgb color, push the center coordinates and radius, draw an arc from zero to three hundred sixty degrees, and fill it. Finally, output a show page command and an end of file indicator. Return the complete string.

title: M3U Playlist Generator
spec: Write a function `generate(playlist)` that creates an extended audio playlist format string. The input contains a master title, a creator name, an export date, a software version, a default genre, and a list of track objects. Begin the string with a header line combining the extended playlist marker and the software version. Follow this with a descriptive comment line showing the master title, creator, and export date. Add a global tag line specifying the default genre for the list. For each track, output a runtime information line containing the track duration in seconds, the artist name, and the song title. Below that, output the file path by combining the track folder, file name, and file extension. Additionally, output a custom tag line for each track showing its file size in megabytes and audio bitrate. At the end of the file, append a summary comment stating the total number of tracks. Finally, append another comment calculating and displaying the total playlist duration in minutes. Example input includes a creator named Alice, a software version of two point zero, and a track with two hundred seconds.

title: G Code Script Builder
spec: Write a function `slice(job)` that outputs machine instructions for a three dimensional printer. The input provides a material name, measurement units, target temperatures for the printing bed and extruder nozzle, a print speed multiplier, and a list of movement steps. Initialize the file with a comment declaring the material name and the print speed multiplier. Add a command to set the measurement units. Construct a command to set and wait for the bed temperature. Construct another command to set and wait for the nozzle temperature. Add a homing command that resets the machine axes specified in a homing list parameter. Loop through the movement steps, outputting a linear move command that specifies the x, y, and z coordinates along with the movement speed. If a step involves pushing plastic, build a dedicated extrusion command specifying the extrusion amount and speed. Include a fan speed command if the step specifies a cooling percentage. Finish the script with a concluding comment reporting the total number of movement steps processed. Example input includes a material name of plastic, measurement units of millimeters, and a bed temperature of sixty.

title: Conky Status Text Generator
spec: Write a function `configure(settings)` that generates a text based configuration for a desktop system monitor. The input holds layout preferences like alignment, update interval in seconds, font family, font size, a base hexadecimal color, a network interface name, a disk path, and a processor core count. Output the initial configuration block setting the alignment and the update interval variables. Add a configuration line establishing the font family and font size. Add a color line applying the base hexadecimal color. Construct a text block that displays system metrics. Include a processor usage line showing the total processor core count and current global utilization percentage. Add a memory usage line displaying used memory, maximum memory, and percentage. Add a disk usage line pointing to the provided disk path, showing space used and total capacity. Conclude with a network line showing download and upload speeds for the provided network interface name. Finish with an uptime line indicating the days and hours the system has been running. Example input provides an update interval of two seconds, a font family of Arial, and a network interface name of ethernet zero.

title: BBCode Forum Post Builder
spec: Write a function `format(post)` that translates a structured post into bulletin board code. The input contains a main title, a font size, an author name, a text body, a quote source, a quoted message, an image web address, an image width, a target web link, a link label, and a signature text. Start by rendering the main title in bold and wrapping it in a size tag specifying the chosen font size. Display the text body inside standard paragraph tags. Render the quoted message inside a quote tag that specifically attributes the quote source in its parameter. Render the image web address using an image tag that specifies the exact pixel width in its attribute. Render the target web link using a url tag, placing the web address in the tag attribute and the link label inside the tag. Render a warning section that wraps a predefined warning text in color tags specifying a red color. Add a horizontal rule, and then render the signature text colored in gray. Append a footer mentioning the author name and the current date. Example input includes a main title of Announcements, a font size of twenty, and an author name of Admin.

title: MUD Room Description Formatter
spec: Write a function `describe(room)` that builds a text representation of a virtual environment for a multiplayer text game. The input includes a room name, zone name, environmental narrative, light level, a weather condition, a list of exit directions, a list of active player names, a list of items on the floor, and a danger level identifier. Display the room name and zone name wrapped in square brackets. Print the environmental narrative followed by a sentence stating the current light level and weather condition. Format the danger level identifier inside a warning sentence about the area. Format the exit directions as a comma separated list enclosed in brackets. Include a sentence noting the total number of active players currently in the area before listing their names. Create a sentence listing the players currently standing in the room. For each item on the floor, output a distinct sentence stating that the specific item rests on the ground. Finally, append a prompt line asking the user what action they want to take in the room name. Example input includes a room name of Dark Cave, a zone name of Underworld, and a light level of pitch black.

title: System Information ASCII Layout
spec: Write a function `fetch(system)` that produces a terminal status screen string. The input contains a username, hostname, operating system name, operating system version, kernel version, days and hours of uptime, package count, package manager name, shell name, display width, display height, and desktop environment name. Construct a top banner combining the username and hostname separated by an at symbol. Create a line for the operating system combining the name and version. Create a line for the kernel version. Construct an uptime line showing the days and hours. Build a package line combining the total package count and the package manager used. Add a line for the shell name. Build a screen resolution line showing the display width and display height. Add a line for the desktop environment. Conclude with a system memory line calculating the percentage of memory used out of a total amount. Example input includes a username of admin, an operating system name of Linux, and a package count of one thousand.

title: Asterisk Dialplan Context Builder
spec: Write a function `dialplan(context)` that creates a telephone routing script. The input specifies a context name, a primary extension number, a caller identification name, a greeting sound file, a destination technology, a destination peer, a timeout value, and a voicemail box identifier. Start the output by wrapping the context name in square brackets. Write a step to answer the call at the given extension. Add a step to set the caller identification name variable for the extension. Add a step to play back the greeting sound file. Create a dial step combining the destination technology, destination peer, and timeout value. Include a step to log a warning message to the console containing the primary extension number. Include a step to route the call to the specified voicemail box if the dial fails. Finish with a step to hang up the call at the given extension. Example input includes a context name of incoming, a primary extension number of one hundred, and a destination technology of session initiation protocol.

title: File System Table Generator
spec: Write a function `mounts(drives)` that builds a disk mounting configuration file. The input contains a machine hostname, a backup server address, a backup path, a swap partition device, a temporary folder size, and a list of volume objects containing device identifiers and mount point directories. Begin the file with a comment line indicating it was generated for the provided machine hostname. Output a swap entry using the swap partition device. Output a temporary file system entry specifying the temporary folder size in the options. Output a network file system entry combining the backup server address and backup path as the source. Include a read only network entry combining the backup server address and a public share path. Loop through the volume objects, and for each one, output a descriptive comment naming the mount point directory. Then, output a line with the device identifier, mount point directory, and default options. Finally, append a concluding comment stating the total number of physical volumes processed. Example input includes a machine hostname of server one, a swap partition device of slash dev slash sdb, and a temporary folder size of four gigabytes.

title: Lilypond Music Notation Builder
spec: Write a function `score(sheet)` that generates a sheet music engraving script. The input specifies a syntax version string, song title, composer name, arranger name, instrument name, time signature numerator, time signature denominator, clef type, base tempo, and a sequence of notes. Begin the script by declaring the syntax version enclosed in quotes. Build a header block defining the song title, composer name, and arranger name inside quotes. Open a score block and a new staff block, specifying the instrument name in the staff properties. Output a time command using the time signature numerator and denominator. Output a clef command with the chosen clef type in quotes. Output a tempo command setting a quarter note equal to the base tempo. List the sequence of notes inside a relative pitch block. Finally, append a custom footer line displaying a copyright notice with the composer name. Example input includes a song title of Moonlight Sonata, a composer name of Beethoven, and a time signature numerator of four.

title: RPG Character Stat Sheet Printer
spec: Write a function `print(character)` that formats a textual record for a role playing game participant. The input provides a participant name, title, numerical level, species, profession, current and maximum health, current and maximum magic, gold count, weapon name, weapon damage, armor name, and armor defense. Output a top header bounding the participant name and title with equal signs. Print a secondary header combining the numerical level, species, and profession. Format a vital statistics line showing current health over maximum health and current magic over maximum magic. Display a wealth line indicating the gold count. Create a combat summary line displaying the combined total of weapon damage and armor defense. Display an offensive equipment line stating the weapon name and its damage value. Display a defensive equipment line stating the armor name and its defense value. Finish the sheet with a summary sentence declaring that the participant name is ready for adventure. Example input provides a participant name of Arthur, a numerical level of ten, and a profession of Knight.

title: YARA Malware Rule Generator
spec: Write a function `detect(signature)` that generates a threat hunting rule block. The input includes a rule identifier, author name, description, creation date, file size limit in kilobytes, a primary threat string, a secondary threat string, and an integer for the minimum match count. Start by declaring the rule using the rule identifier and opening a brace. Inside the meta section, assign the author name, description, and creation date into quoted string fields on separate lines. In the strings section, assign the primary threat string to a variable named dollar sign primary, formatted in quotes. Assign the secondary threat string to a variable named dollar sign secondary, formatted in quotes. In the condition section, write a rule demanding that the file size is less than the limit. Write another condition requiring that at least the minimum match count of the defined strings are found in the file. Finally, close the rule block with a brace. Example input includes a rule identifier of Trojan Dropper, an author name of Analyst, and a file size limit of five hundred kilobytes.

title: Openbox Window Manager Menu Builder
spec: Write a function `menu(config)` that builds an extensible markup language file for a desktop application menu. The input holds a root menu identifier, a root menu label, a terminal application command, a web browser command, a file manager command, a text editor command, a separator label, and an exit command. Output the opening tag for the menu, inserting the identifier and label into their respective attributes. Create an item tag and execution action for the terminal application command, placing it inside a command tag. Create a similar execution block for the web browser command. Create a third execution block for the file manager command. Create a fourth execution block for the text editor command. Output a separator tag specifying the separator label in its attribute.
